705.33: 3 o'clock. Here you go. Are you alright with Earl Grey?
705.34: 4 o'clock. I know it's a little early, but would you like some biscuits? I baked them.
705.35: 5 o'clock. Shall I make more Earl Grey? This pot has gotten a bit cold. Ah, I don't have to? You will? Thanks.
705.36: 6 o'clock. Good morning. You need to get up, too. Come on, a new day is starting.
705.37: 7 o'clock. Here, have some of my special English breakfast. Here's some freshly made bread with plenty of butter and marmalade. I made the marmalade myself, too. How is it?
705.38: 8 o'clock. Now that we're done with breakfast, it's time to gather the fleet. Let's get to work.
705.39: 9 o'clock. Hi, Ark. You're looking well today, too. Let's form a fleet again.
705.40: 10 o'clock. Eh? Ark, what did you say? ...Eh? Swordfish? ...Ah, well, I can carry the seaplane version... No no, I can't carry those... No, really...
705.41: 11 o'clock. Well, the Swordfish certainly are fine machines. They were unrivaled in the Atlantic. Yep.
705.42: Midday. Now, it's time for lunch. Here, have a meat pie. It's good, right? I made this, too. Go on, finish it.
705.43: 1 o'clock. Ah, Admiral, would you like another meat pie? Really? Don't hold back.
705.44: 2 o'clo- Huh!? Is that... Is that the battleship Bismarck!? She's here? Oh no, Ark, come quickly. Send the Swordfish here!
705.45: 3 o'clock. Is that so? She's an ally now... Ah, so that's why. Th-then let's have afternoon tea together. Yes, we can invite Eugen too... Wait, what? Is she really here too? ...She is...
705.46: 4 o'clock. What a fright. What's going on here?
705.47: 5 o'clock. Ark, Bismarck, and Eugen are all here and are allies. It's throwing me for a spin. Eh? "Look at the sunset"? Ah, yes. The sun is setting. What about it?
705.48: 6 o'clock. What shall we have for dinner? Should I make something? Admiral, what would you like to eat? How about lamb chops? I'm good at making that.
705.49: 7 o'clock. Thanks for waiting. Here's my special lamb chops. Is some scotch fine with you?
705.50: 8 o'clock. Well, Admiral? Was it good? ...I see. Then I'll make it for you again.
705.51: 9 o'clock. Those small light cruisers cause a ruckus every single night, don't they? It's a bit of a bother. Admiral, aren't you going to reprimand them? Oh. Well, that's fine then.
705.52: 10 o'clock. Ah, Nelson, what's the matter? Gah, you reek of booze. You really went overboard. Eh? I don't want any. Take your rum and go. And you! That's enough drinking!
705.53: 11 o'clock. Whew, another day is finally over. Everything that happened today really wore me out. Good work. You should lie down and have a short rest.

965.1: You are mon amiral? Bonjour! I am the La Galissonniêre-class light cruiser Gloire! I love the tricolor... but it's a bit flashy... Is it alright if I try something else on later?
965.25: I'm the French-born La Galissonnière-class light cruiser, Gloire. I was part of many different fleets, but became part of the Allied forces after Dakar. I was then remodelled in New York. I am a light cruiser bearing the name "Glory". Please remember my story!
965.2: Mon Amiral? Oh, so the title is "Admiral" here. I'll remember that.
965.3: Glory? Honour? No, I fight for the fleet and for everyone in it.
965.4: Pardon? What is it? Is this about my uniform? Well, I think it's good for peacetime, but better to change out during dangerous times of war. I have another outfit in mind, if you give me a moment. Fufu.
965.29: Oh, Haruna-san, welcome! Mhm, yeah. Fufu, really? I went through a lot myself. Yeah, right!? After that I was put up in New York. We all went through so much, didn't we.
965.28: Mon Amiral, over here, over here. I tried my hand at making canelés. How is it? Delicious, right? I have some café au lait for you as well, enjoy.
965.24: Mon Amiral, what's with the serious look on your face? Eh? This is for me? Oh it's wonderful! I'm honoured, mon Amiral. This is the most glorious moment in my life. Merci beaucoup! I love you.
965.8: Information? Please wait. Gloire shall bring it to you.
965.13: Fourth Cruiser Division, light cruiser Gloire, leaving port. Come now, let's head out to sea.
965.5: A new ship. How wonderful, she's positively glowing.
965.7: The fleet has returned to port. Ufufu.
965.14: Force Y, Gloire, sortieing. Don't let your guard down, everyone. Shall we?
965.15: Gloire reporting: enemy detected. Please prepare for combat. Let's proceed carefully.
965.18: As a light cruiser, at times like these I must go!
965.23: There we go! I'm number one? Ufufu, mon Amiral... Merci!
965.21: Now you've done it! You won't so easily be forgiven...
965.22: I... could I be... sinking? Water... water's getting in... Adieu, mon Amiral...

970.1: Bonjour, mon Amiral! I am the La Galissonnière-class light cruiser Gloire! This outfit is nice, right? I've come to like it. Let's have a good time today.
970.2: Admiral? No, mon Amiral? Is that okay? I'm sorta used to it.
970.3: Glory? Honour? No, I fight for the fleet and everyone in it, including you.
970.4: Pardon? What is it? Is this about my uniform? It's nice and plain, isn't it? I like it. Eh, you think it's actually not plain at all? Hmm, is that so? But even Japan's fast battleships- that's not the same?
970.14: La Galissonnière-class Gloire, sortieing. Don't let your guard down, everyone. Shall we?
970.18: As a light cruiser, I must fight even at night. Now, I must go!
970.19: Ahh, geez! Does this camo even work!?
970.30: Mon Amiral, the clock has struck midnight. Today I, Gloire, will be of service. Let us begin.
970.31: Mon Amiral, it's 1 am. Are you sleepy? You okay? Sure? Should I make some café au lait?
970.32: Mon Amiral, it's 2 am. I'll do the rest of the paperwork. Please go ahead and take a break. Yes, leave it to me.
970.33: Mon Amiral, it's 3am. Hehe, you're such a cute sleeper. Bonne nuit, mon Amiral...
970.34: Ah, you're awake, mon Amiral? Don't worry, the paperwork is all done. It's... 4 am, almost morning.
970.35: Bonjour, Mon Amiral! It's 5 am. It's looking like another fine morning. See, even the birds are singing. Here, your café au lait, enjoy.
970.36: Mon Amiral, it's 6 am. I'll wake everyone up. Fleet, all hands, assemble! All hands, assemble! Good morning!
970.37: Mon Amiral, it's 7 am. Here's your breakfast. Freshly baked croissant and cafe au lait with plenty of milk. Bon appétit!
970.38: Mon Amiral, it's 8 am. Ah, Commandant Teste-san, good morning. You're always up so early! I'll be right out too.
970.39: Mon Amiral, it's 9 am. Now, let's head out to sea. Oh, Mogador-san, good morning. If you'd excuse us. Weighing anchor!
970.40: Mon Amiral, it's 10 am. Richelieu-san, you look fantastic again today! Good morning. Yes, let's keep it up today.
970.41: Mon Amiral, it's 11 am- Ah, that's...? Do you know, Richelieu-san? She's the Japan fleet's Yamato-san? Amazing...
970.42: Mon Amiral, it's noon. I got this "onigiri" from the Japan fleet. What a strange snack. Might as well try it then? Nom.
970.43: Mon Amiral, I really like this Japan "onigiri". The one with grilled salmon is especially delicious. Eh? I'm supposed to eat these with my hands? No way, without a fork? Ah, the time is 1 pm.
970.44: Mon Amiral, it's 2- Ah, Japan's Haruna-san, good work today. Your main battery camouflage is still as gorgeous as ever. Eh, me too? No, mine still has a long way to go...
970.45: Mon Amiral, it's 3 pm. Indeed, I don't know how effective this camouflage is, but I've grown to like it. Haruna-san, would you... like to try full-body camo?
970.46: Oh my, Comandante Cappellini? You're still up to your old tricks then? Really? We've been through a lot, haven't we? Well, that was a long time ago. Mhm, right. It's 4 pm, almost evening.
970.47: Mon Amiral, look. The sunset is... beau-ti-ful... It's 5pm. Let's head back to the port. Aren't you tired? I'll make dinner tonight.
970.48: Mon Amiral, it's 6 pm. I'm making dinner now, please wait a moment. Would you like some wine first? Same here, ufufu.
970.49: Cooking in the kitchen with wine in one hand is so fun! Here, the quiche is already done. To go with the drinks, of course. Cheers! It's 7 pm.
970.50: Mon Amiral, it's 8pm. Here we go! True pot-au-feu from France! Bon appétit! It's amazing, isn't it? Completely different from the one you have here in Japan.
970.51: It's 9 pm! What's better than drinking and cooking with the people you love, right? Hey, mon Amiral, should I open another bottle of wine? Or was that enough? Good, I'm opening another! How about a red?
970.52: Drunk already, mon Amiral? Kay, look riiiight here, on my camo, how many black linesss? Hmm? Nahhhh, come on, get closer and cooount! Huh? The time? Ah, guessss it's 10 pm, but who caresss?
970.53: Whew, merci. All that water helped me sober up. How does the Japanese saying go? "Don't let the drink drink you?" It's already 11 pm. Mon Amiral, thank you for today. Please take care of me tomorrow too, alright? Bonne nuit.

1001.1: So you are the Admiral, sir? Very well! Kirov-class light cruiser, Kirov. I will lend my power to you, sir. I'm counting on you.
1001.25: I was the first of the Kirov-class cruisers, built by the navy of a country in the north with Italian technical assistance. I was built as a new-generation Soviet cruiser and deployed with the Baltic Fleet. I supported the army during the Siege of Leningrad and contributed to the city's defence. My service record is one full of shore bombardments.
1001.3: You ought to add me to the battle line. Why this gratuitous display of gratitude? Vodka would be enough.
1001.4: Oh, you're interested in my camouflage? Very well, you may come closer and inspect it. As someone built with Italian technology, I... Sir, where are you looking...? That is not part of my rigging! Do you wish to be shot at point blank?
1001.29: Admiral seems to be occupied. Very well. I'll pay a visit to "the sky-blue cruiser", that destroyer who's let her nickname get to her head - she's not here? Hello? Anyone? Hm? You're... A Japanese heavy cruiser? Oh! What's that sake? Daruma? Oh, well I'll have a sip... It's not bad. Not bad at all! Alright, let's drink! You're not going home tonight!
1001.28: What's wrong, sir? Are you tired? You need some vodka. Cheers! Feeling better yet? What? Now you're sleepy!? Fine, I'll lend you my shoulder for a bit. Just a bit, okay?
1001.24: What is it, sir? You're offering me this to me? My sir, you do have an eye for these things. Not bad. I'll take it. I love you too.
1001.8: Here is a report. Read it, Admiral. They say information is life.
1001.13: I, Kirov, shall take charge of the fleet. Follow my lead. All hands, on deck!
1001.9: My main battery is good, although it has a few problems.
1001.10: But the treaty? I'm unaware of any. None apply to me!
1001.27: Thank you. You have my gratitude.
1001.11: Sorry, I'm not feeling well. Pardon me a moment.
1001.12: I've taken major damage and must take bed rest. Sorry.
1001.5: It seems that a new ship has joined us. Which one?
1001.7: We're back at port. A toast to that.
1001.14: Baltic Fleet - sorry, Northern Fleet flagship, Kirov-class cruiser, Kirov, weighing anchor. Follow me!
1001.15: Enemy spotted. Let's tear them apart. Fleet, prepare for battle! Hurrah!
1001.17: Fire! Fire until the shells are red hot! Fire, fire!
1001.18: A night battle then. I accept. Your opponent shall be me.
1001.23: I am receiving the honours for this battle? Very well, I accept. Thank you very much.
1001.20: Ouch... You bastards don't know what you've done! Counterattack, now!
1001.21: Uwaaah! You've really done it now! Bastards! I'll remember this!
1001.22: Oh, so you've sunk me in battle. So be it. I see now... Goodbye.

1006.1: Admiral, hello. Cruiser Kirov is in position. I'm counting on you today.
1006.2: Admiral, I shall go as well.
1006.3: The battle line looks well-organised. Not bad. A vodka toast, to victory at dawn.

471.1: I've kept you waiting, Commander. First ship of the Kamikaze-class destroyers, Kamikaze, has arrived. Are you ready, everyone? Follow me.
471.25: I am the first of the Kamikaze-class Destroyers, Kamikaze. I am the nameship of a fleet of destroyers designed during the Eight-Eight Fleet Program era. We may be an older model compared to the Mutsuki-class, but I managed to run through that battle to the very end. I hope you'll remember who we are.
471.2: Commander, did you call me? I am prepared.
471.3: I'm an old type? Silly you. A destroyer's capabilities aren't about her specs.
471.4: Stop it, Harukaze. I'm not fond of such things... eh? It's you, Commander. What's the meaning of this? I desire an explanation.
471.29: Destroyer-1? Ah, I was once called that a long time ago. But I am now Kamikaze! That's my nameship! Be sure to remember it!
471.28: Commander, you look tired. Okay, I'll pour something warm for you to drink. One moment, please. Here you go. So, are you warming up? Really? That's a relief.
471.24: Yes, Commander? Another escort mission? I don't mind that... Eh, no? What is that on your hand? It's... for me? Wow, really? Thank you. I'll treasure it... I will treasure it for sure!
471.8: Looking at intel? It is vital. I'm glad that you're an able Commander.
471.13: Destroyer Division 1 Flagship, Kamikaze. It's time to weigh anchor!
471.9: Am I getting stronger? Th-Thank you. I'm glad, but...
471.10: Mm, this is good. I can survive till the very end with this. Thank you.
471.27: Right. Refueling complete! What's next? Fleet escort?
471.11: Just a little... let me rest a little. No peeking. I'll be done in an instant.
471.12: Ahh... this is awful in many ways. Commander, I'm taking a break for a while. Hurm...
471.5: New ship construction has completed. Good!
471.7: Commander, the fleet has returned. In any case, I'm glad that they're all okay.
471.14: Flagship Kamikaze, setting sail. Are you ready, everyone? Follow me.
471.15: Enemy fleet spotted. Right, ready for battle. On me, everyone.
471.18: Pursuing the enemy fleet. Battle speed 5. Charge! Follow me!
471.23: Yes! Ah, but please don't praise me. I'm only doing my usual routine. T-that's right.
471.21: I'm hit? Where? I-I won't sink!
471.22: No way. It can't be! I'm filling with water... No...

476.1: Commander, I'll do my best! First ship of the Kamikaze-class destroyers, Kamikaze, has arrived. Let's face our battles head-on!
476.4: Is that Ashigara? I'm a bit busy right now... Eh? Commander!? What's the meaning of this? I would like an explanation of what it is you think you're doing.
476.9: You're going to make me stronger? Thanks. Don't forget the anti-sub equipment!
476.10: Huh? It's for a transport mission? I guess. Actually, I'd rather not remove my torpedoes...
476.14: Even if the war outlook is bad, we've got to do something! Flagship Kamikaze, setting sail. Fleet, weigh anchor!
476.30: Right! Today I'll be taking care of you as your secretary. Is that ok? It is now 12 midnight. Leave the hourly announcements to me!
476.31: 0100. *yawn* I'm a bit sleepy... but I'll be fine. You can rely on me.
476.32: 0200. It's the hour of Ushimitsu. What? You're scared, Commander? Guess you do have an adorable side.
476.33: 0300. Umm... do you feel like... going to the washroom? I'll accompany you there. How's that...?
476.34: 0400. Oh, thank goodness. It's going to be morning. Eh? The night? I don't... find it... scary...
476.35: 0500. That's not it! I'm completely fine on the ocean. It's not the same as night time on dry land. Geez...
476.36: 0600. Commander, I'll be performing the morning call. Fleet, arise! It's morning. The morning has arrived. Rise and shine, everyone!
476.37: 0700. Right! Commander, allow me to cook. Wait a moment, please... Okay! Sorry to keep you waiting. I had to watch the barley rice.
476.38: 0800. What do you think of my cooking? Mmm! Right! So, after this, let's begin with fleet operations.
476.39: 0900. What shall we start with this morning? Expeditions? Quests? Mmm, I can't decide with such a wonderful fleet. Commander, what do you think?
476.40: 1000. Right! Now then, we should begin with an expedition. Put me in charge of a convoy escort. Hey! I can say with confidence that I won't return with less than one shou's worth.
476.41: 1100. Geez, it's almost lunch time... what should I do? I don't mind cooking again, but... how about cooking together? It can be the commander's solemn duty, mmm?
476.42: 1200. Okay, I've decided. We'll have salted rice balls for lunch... is that ok? I'll prepare some miso soup to go with it. It matches with the salty flavor.
476.43: 1300. How was it? Lunch, I mean. There's a shortage of vegetables. Fresh vegetables have gotten so expensive.
476.44: 1400. Didn't my salted rice balls turn out well? What? Did it take long to make...? ...Ah, no, not at all! I am very efficient cook.
476.45: 150— Ah, Haguro! Thank you for your hard work. You look great... eh... ah... Well, I'm feeling great too. Look, look! I'm fine!
476.46: 1600. A transport operation? Right, then. Though I do feel a little worried without torpedoes... I'll be fine, so don't worry!
476.47: 1700. Ah, Commander, the sun is setting. How beautiful... this reminds me of the sunset I saw in Singapore. It's nostalgic. Is Nokaze... all right?
476.48: 1800. Commander, it's past sunset, isn't it? The fleet has returned to port? Let me cook dinner, then. Please look forward to it.
476.49: 1900... Here, Commander! Kamikaze special pork miso soup with fresh vegetables. It'll go well with the barley rice. Bon appetite!
476.50: 20— Oh!? Ashigara? Mmm, mmm... You are preparing pork cutlet curry rice here? Wow, that's wonderful... Commander, can you eat? Ah, you ate it. That's great.
476.51: 2100. Mmmmmm... delicious. Ashigara, thank you for the victory pork cutlet curry rice. *sigh* I overate.
476.52: 2200. Eh... Commander, what is it? What makes me feel afraid? Mmm... submarines are a nightmare for a convoy escort, you know? Eh, you don't believe me?
476.53: 2300. I can't do it! Submarines are terrifying. Of course, any enemy is horrible... Night time? The sea at night is not so frightening.

472.1: Morning. It's Asakaze. Second ship of the Kamikaze-class destroyers, Asakaze. Commander? Please memorize it soon. Okay?
472.25:
Kamikaze-class destroyer, second ship, Asakaze. I was born in Nagasaki.

Along with my younger sister Harukaze and the others, I formed the historic Fifth Destroyer Division. I was naturally the flagship. I took part in landing operations in the early stages of the war. Of course, I was also reliable and punctual with convoy escorts.

Mm! If it was there, I did it!
472.3: Yes...? A fleet escort...? Leave it to me, if you would, please. It'll be fine.
472.4: D... W-What are- Don't make a fool of me! Eh? You're not... trying to...? Ah... sorry. I misunderstood. Right! That makes us even!
472.29: I'm so bored... Harukaze, doesn't talking like that put you to sleep? I mean, look at Matsukaze. Ah... Matsukaze, you're wearing that hat again. It'll get in the way in battle, so take it off. Ah... what? What's that? You're picking a fight with your big sis? Bring it on! I'm not going to hold back!
472.28: What's this? You're so undisciplined. You're worn out from this? *sigh* Commander, haven't you lacked motivation recently? I have no choice, then. I'll help you get your fighting spirit back. Look this way for a moment. Ready? Close your eyes. ...Ah, they opened! You opened your eyes! I'm not doing this anymore!
472.24: What is it, Commander? To call me out to a place like this... I'm very busy right now. Well, with fleet escorts and such. Convoys and such. Eh? What's this? For me...? W-Well...! I suppose I'll accept it. I-It's beautiful... and the size is just right...
472.8: Hm? The intelligence? I'll go get it for you. Hold on.
472.13: Fifth Destroyer Division, setting sail! Ready? Everyone, follow me!
472.10: How is it...? Well, anything would work well on me!
472.27: Well, I'll have some. It's essential.
472.11: Sorry. Is it okay if I fall back for a bit?
472.12:
Hmm... I'm sure Kamikaze-nee is going to scold me for this...
Well, I suppose I don't have to tell her?
472.7:
Commander? The fleet has returned. *whew* I'm so tired...
Would you mind massaging my shoulders?
472.14: DesRon 5, heading out! All DesDiv 5 members, are you ready? Sortieing!
472.15: So the enemy fleet was spotted? Everyone ready? Let's do this.
472.18: DesRon 5, charging in. Fall into formation behind me! We're going in!
472.17: Yes! You took the bait. I'll finish you!
472.23: Please observe! I, Asakaze, am the greatest. My eloquence and training are on a whole other level! Uh...? Commander? Why are you laughing? What's with you!?
472.21: It's not as if I took a torpedo! This isn't... enough to sink me!
472.22:
It can't be... I'm... sinking once again...
Matsukaze... where are...? Please come and... find me...

370.1: Morning. It's Asakaze. Second ship of the Kamikaze-class destroyers, Asakaze. Commander, have you come to appreciate the morning? You already liked it? Ehe♪ ...Alright!
370.13: First Surface Escort Division, heading out! Harukaze, are you ready? We're going to protect everyone this time! Don't let the enemy subs come near them! Sortie!
370.10: Isn't this nice? Commander, have you come to understand me a little?
370.27: Of course I'll have some. Let's keep at it!
370.14: DesRon 5, heading out! Is everyone ready? Matsukaze? If you fall behind, I won't let you hear the end of it!
370.23: Please observe! I, Asakaze, am the greatest, am I not? Well, haven't I known the Commander for a long time? And my training is on a whole other level! Uh...? Commander? Why are you still laughing? What's with you!?
370.30: Midnight. *whew* I'll be the one to accompany you today. ...What? Is there a problem? ...Oh, so I see. Then I guess it's fine.
370.31: 2 a.m.! Er... what, you want it the other way? How pretentious... Well, whatever. Aye! 0100. Is that fine?
370.32: 3 a-! ...Oh, right... 0200. Well, I guess it's fine. It's 02. 02. Hey, are you even listening?
370.33: 0300. Commander, you're not even listening, right? If you're not listening, I'm-going-to-stop. He~ey!? ...Ah, you reacted. I guess you were listening.
370.34: 0400. *stretch* It's finally morning...! Morning, morning. Hmhm♪ I love mornings! Mornings are really nice, you know? Right, Commander?
370.35: 0500. It's here! The morning! It's morning! The morning breeze feels so good~♪ Right, Commander? ...Eh? Close the window because it's cold? *sigh* ...Our Commander really doesn't get it at all.
370.36: 0600. We're going full throttle this morning. First of all, you have to start the day with a delicious breakfast! I cooked up a huuge batch of barley rice. Now, eat up!
370.37: 0700. Commander, what's this? You haven't gotten through much of your meal at all! No, no, this won't do at all! You have to eat properly in the morning. Here— a big helping of barley rice! ...It can't be helped. I'll give you some of my pickled radish.
370.38: 0800. We're going to start the morning exercises. Div 5, form up! Hatakaze? Harukaze? Matsukaze? ...Oh well. We'll do the morning exercises with those who showed up. Destroyer Division 5, we're setting sail this morning!
370.39: 0900. *whew* I worked up a good morning sweat! Alright! It's still morning, so let's keep going! What's next? An expedition? A sortie?
370.40: 1000. Uuu... Morning is ending... However, we're still in the a.m. hours! It's technically morning! Wh-Why are you eying me like that, Matsukaze!? What is it?
370.41: 1100. I get it already. I suppose it is almost lunchtime. I ate quite a lot in the morning, but I'm already getting an appetite. And you, Commander...?
370.42: 1200. It's noon. Hm? Harukaze, what is that? ...Eh? A sandwich? What's that? Destroyers should eat barley rice! Right, Commander? ...H-Huh? You don't feel that way?
370.43: 1300. Hmmm... Sandwiches aren't bad, but they're not something I'd eat too often. Still, thank you, Harukaze. Thanks for the meal!
370.44: 140- Ah, Mogami-san, Mikuma-san. Hi there. Um... what's that you have? Eh? A model? Hmmm... so you build them. Eh~ how eccentric. ...Ah! No, I didn't mean it like that! If it comes out okay, would you show it to me?
370.45: 1500. Well, I guess everyone has their hobbies. Matsukaze, what do you do on your days off? ...Eh? Ahh... I see. Fu... how eccentric. It's fine, though.
370.46: 1600. Ah, Nowaki? What's up? Ah, I see. Nah, I haven't seen her. Right, got it. If I see her, I'll let you know.
370.47: 1700. And so it ended up being evening. Eh? What about the sunset...? Ha! What are you talking about? The morning sunrise is many times more lovely. Right?
370.48: 1800. Ah, geez, after saying all that, it's already night— night! Night is somehow... How to put it... I have no motivation.
370.49: 1900. Commander, well~ ...I know it's wrong, but I don't really feel like working at night... ...Eh? You're ordering takeout for dinner? Ah, then I wanna order something! Umm... I'll have...
370.50: 2000. Mmm... even Mamiya's takeout is delicious. I'm so full! Treating ourselves can be nice sometimes. Every day would be... hmm... that would be quite the luxury, huh? Yeah.
370.51: 21... 00. ...Night is... I don't like the night. I especially dislike the sea at night. I like mornings. I like being out on the sea. I like the clear blue skies. Eh? DesRon 3? No, I'm a part of DesRon 5.
370.52: 22... 00. The First Surface Escort Division? ...Yeah. I fought hard, but... I wanted to protect them, but... it was too intense. That's why I hate the night.
370.53: 23... 00. It's well into the night. There's no avoiding it, though. ...It's fine! The morning sun will always rise again. Hey, Commander? Let's do our best tomorrow morning!

473.1: My name is Harukaze, third ship of the Kamikaze-class destroyers. Commander-sama, I am pleased to make your acquaintance.
473.25: I am Harukaze, the third ship of the Kamikaze-class destroyers. I was born in Maizuru. I used to be called Destroyer-5, but I later got a real name, "Harukaze". I was in Destroyer Division 5 and also belonged to the first Maritime Escort Flotilla, in which I helped protect everyone. Even if the fighting ends... I will still protect you.

922.25: I'm the 12th of Ukuru-class coastal defense ship, Inagi. When I was born, the balance of forces was already heavily tilted to the enemy's advantage, but I served on naval escort missions on the surviving shipping lanes. I escorted a convoy in the Hokkaido area and then did it in the Tohoku area too. Later, while temporarily anchored at Hachinohe, I was engaged by planes from the enemy task force. There were no more friendly fighters in the sky, and later, people called me the "The Shield of Hachinohe", I heard.
922.3: Do you need something from me?

922.29: Well... those enemy fighters were already fighter-bombers. Both machine-gun fire and concentrated rocket fire – it was so terrifying. But I'll fight. If there's meaning to it, then there's no other choice. If you'd been there, you would have done the same, right?
